equation_request.abstract: Quantum walks on translation invariant regular graphs spread quadratically faster than their classical counterparts. The same coherence that gives them this quantum speedup inhibits, or even stops their spread in the presence of disorder. We ask how to create an efficient transport channel from a fixed source site (A) to fixed target site (B) in a disordered 2-dimensional discrete-time quantum walk by cutting some of the links. We show that the somewhat counterintuitive strategy of cutting links along a single line connecting A to B creates such a channel. The efficient transport along the cut is due to topologically protected chiral edge states, which exist even though the bulk Chern number in this system vanishes. We give a realization of the walk as a periodically driven lattice Hamiltonian, and identify the bulk topological invariant responsible for the edge states as the quasienergy winding of this Hamiltonian.

specification.problem: Reconstruct a minimal model of a 2D discrete-time quantum walk (DTQW) with link cuts and disorder, to study transport from site A to site B along a line of cut links. The abstract gives only qualitative claims, so only generic background walk dynamics are specified.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance: a generic split-step DTQW on a small L x L periodic square lattice with a 4-state coin, a cut line of removed links, and a site-dependent disorder phase. Out of scope: the paper's actual walk operator, disorder model, cut geometry, Floquet Hamiltonian realization, quasienergy winding invariant calculation, and edge-state proof.

symbols.meaning: Conditional shift that reflects (stays in place with flipped direction) on cut links
symbols.domain: unitary on position and coin space

symbols.meaning: Probability at B after t steps

equations.label: Walk step
equations.description: One step of the DTQW: coin, disorder phase, then shift.
equations.justification: Abstract names a disordered 2D DTQW but gives no operator; this is a generic proposed form.
assumptions: Operator ordering and the form of disorder are assumed

equations.label: Disorder
equations.justification: Simplest disorder model; the paper's model is not given in the abstract.

equations.label: Shift with cut links
equations.description: Shift hops along intact links and reflects at cut links, where \bar{c} is the opposite direction.
equations.justification: Abstract states links are cut; the reflecting-boundary implementation is an assumption.
assumptions: Cut links are the set along a line from A to B

equations.label: Evolution and transport probability
equations.description: State after t steps and probability to be at target B.
equations.justification: Standard definition of discrete-time quantum walk evolution and site probability.

equations.label: Floquet quasienergy
equations.description: Quasienergy eigenproblem for a periodically driven system; the winding invariant is built from the quasienergy bands (details not given).
equations.justification: Abstract mentions a periodically driven Hamiltonian and quasienergy winding; this is only the generic Floquet eigenproblem, not the invariant.

registers.name: pos
registers.role: Position (x,y) in binary encoding, x register first

registers.name: coin
registers.role: Direction index c in binary encoding

specification.initial_state: Assumed localized at source A with a fixed coin state: |\psi_0\rangle=|A\rangle\otimes|c_0\rangle

steps.description: Choose a tiny L, positions A and B, the cut line of links, and a disorder phase sample.
Build U from coin, disorder, and shift with cuts, then apply it t times.
Compute P_B(t) and compare cut versus no-cut cases. Optionally diagonalize U for quasienergies.

specification.measurement: Measure the position register in the computational basis after t steps to estimate P_B(t).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Average P_B(t) over disorder realizations and compare cut versus uncut lattices.
assumptions: Grover coin, periodic boundaries, reflecting cuts and random phase disorder are all proposed choices
The abstract's actual walk is not reproduced
